knowledge_units.context_summary: The study introduces a universal post-preparation method using paraffin coating to enhance photoluminescence in monolayer transition metal dichalcogenides by removing substrate effects. This technique leverages the thermal expansion of paraffin to induce spontaneous fluctuation and desorption of the monolayers. The method is applicable to both sulfur-based (MoS2, WS2) and selenium-based (MoSe2, WSe2) compounds.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The study introduces a paraffin coating method to enhance photoluminescence in monolayer transition metal dichalcogenides by removing substrate effects. This technique is applicable to both sulfur-based and selenium-based compounds, offering a universal strategy where previous chemical treatments were limited. The process involves melting paraffin and applying it via spin coating to induce spontaneous fluctuation and desorption of the monolayer.

attributes.effect: PL enhancement of hundreds of times

relationships.target: packaging flexible light-emitting displays and solar cells

attributes.process: melting paraffin at 80 °C and spin coating
attributes.auxiliary_tool: heat blower to keep paraffin melted

knowledge_units.context_summary: Paraffin coating induces spontaneous deformation and substrate desorption in monolayer transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDCs), leading to significant photoluminescence (PL) enhancement. This effect is observed across sulfur- and selenium-based compounds, with MoS2 showing the highest enhancement factor of 215. The process involves paraffin penetration beneath the monolayer, which removes substrate effects and shifts PL spectra toward exciton-dominated emission.

knowledge_units.context_summary: Paraffin coating induces Raman spectral shifts in monolayer MoS2, indicating strain and reduced carrier concentration due to substrate effect removal. In monolayers surrounded by bulk flakes, paraffin causes in-plane fluctuations and wrinkles rather than full desorption. These strain-induced wrinkles correlate with localized photoluminescence enhancement and peak red-shifts.

knowledge_units.context_summary: Paraffin coating induces spontaneous mechanical stress and deformation in monolayer transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDCs), leading to substrate desorption and significant photoluminescence (PL) enhancement. The mechanism involves strain from paraffin's thermal expansion and the formation of wrinkles or bundles that eliminate substrate effects. This method is applicable to both sulfur- and selenium-based TMDCs, enabling the creation of flexible, transparent optoelectronic devices.

attributes.mechanism: induces mechanical stress via high thermal expansion coefficient

attributes.behavior: spontaneous fluctuation, wrinkle formation, or bundling

components: strain induced by paraffin volume change

relationships.target: PL peak shift to lower energy in folded areas
